overview: White plays 3.h4 in the King's Gambit Accepted, preventing ...g5 and keeping the f4 pawn in doubt. White offers a second pawn for a lead in development and the open f-file and h-file. Black can accept or play ...Nf6 and ...d5 to counter.

white_ideas.idea: Play Nc3, Bc4 and d4 with a big centre

black_ideas.idea: Hold the extra pawn with ...Nf6 or ...Bd6

typical_structures.structure: Open game with the f-pawn gone
White pawns on h4 and e4 against Black's extra f4 pawn

character.notes: Wide open and tactical, with the black pawn on f4 and White's king exposed.

gambit.notes: Black can keep the f4 pawn with ...Nf6 and ...d5.

structure.notes: The f-file and centre are open.

level.notes: Tactical lines need to be known and the line is not first-choice.

sublines_that_differ.name: Standard 3.Nf3
sublines_that_differ.how: the main KGA with the usual g5 fight

character.reason: Gambit lines with exposed kings and open files.

gambit.reason: Black can keep the f4 pawn.

soundness.reason: The rare 3.h4 is thought inferior to the main line.

plans.reason: White pushes the h-pawn and hits the kingside.
